extracted.intended_audience: UK-based scientists applying for Royal Society International Exchanges grants
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and requirements for UK-based researchers applying to the Royal Society's International Exchanges scheme to seed new international research collaborations (one‑off or bilateral visits). Covers eligibility, allowable costs and visit lengths, assessment process, and adjustments for disabled applicants.

rubrics_metrics.name: Alignment with scheme objectives
rubrics_metrics.description: Applications should meet the scheme's objectives: stimulate development of new research collaborations between UK researchers and researchers from around the world; provide seed corn funding to establish partnerships, gather preliminary data, develop research ideas and strengthen applications for further funding; enable UK and international research groups to exchange research staff, to share expertise and exchange ideas.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The scheme is intended to support the formation of new collaborations and early-stage activity (network building, preliminary data), not ongoing established projects. Use the objectives to justify why the proposed activity merits funding.

rubrics_metrics.name: Newness of the collaboration
rubrics_metrics.description: This scheme is not intended to support continued research activities between a UK applicant and a co-applicant who was a former colleague or PhD student or to support other existing or recent collaborations between the applicant and co-applicant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants must demonstrate that the collaboration is new (rather than an ongoing or recently active collaboration). Explain how the project will create a new link or direction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope: single project focus
rubrics_metrics.description: Collaborations should be based on a single project and travel can only take place between the UK and a country/territory where the overseas collaborator is based.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applications should propose a clearly defined single project as the basis for the exchange activity. Multi-country travel or multi-project proposals that do not meet the single-project criterion may be ineligible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligible applicant qualifications
rubrics_metrics.description: You have a PhD or have equivalent research experience.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: State and, where appropriate, evidence your qualification or equivalent experience to satisfy this eligibility requirement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligible employment contract
rubrics_metrics.description: You hold a fixed or permanent contract at an eligible organisation for the duration of the project (ineligible organisations include industrial, private and commercial organisations, university spin-out companies and government bodies).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Confirm your contract type and that your employing organisation is eligible; note that temporary, non-fixed contracts or employment at ineligible organisations will make you ineligible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicant location at time of application
rubrics_metrics.description: You are based in the respective countries/territories at the time of application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants must be physically based in the jurisdiction required (e.g., UK-based applicants for the Royal Society scheme) when applying.

rubrics_metrics.name: Research remit eligibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Your research is within the Royal Society’s remit of natural sciences, which includes but is not limited to biological research and biomedical sciences, chemistry, engineering, mathematics and physics.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Confirm your research falls within the Society’s supported subject groups; consult the breakdown of subject groups and areas supported by the Royal Society in the scheme notes if unclear.

rubrics_metrics.name: Allowable costs
rubrics_metrics.description: Funds can cover travel, subsistence and research expenses.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Budget requests should be limited to these categories and justified in relation to the proposed visits and project activities; see scheme notes for full funding detail.

rubrics_metrics.name: Global rounds funding caps by visit length
rubrics_metrics.description: Global rounds: up to £3,000 for a one-off visit lasting up to three months; up to £6,000 for multiple visits to be completed within one year; up to £12,000 for multiple visits to be completed within two years.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Request amounts must match the visit model and duration proposed. Use these caps when planning the number and duration of visits and justify the requested amounts accordingly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cost Share rounds funding structure and caps
rubrics_metrics.description: Cost Share rounds: grants are available for multiple visits to be completed over a fixed period of two years: up to £12,000 from the Royal Society and an additional up to £12,000 equivalent from the Royal Society’s overseas cost-share funding partner.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cost-share awards require parallel funding arrangements with the named overseas partner; demonstrate the parallel application and confirm the overseas partner’s contribution where applicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cost Share rounds procedural requirement (parallel applications)
rubrics_metrics.description: The UK applicant submits an application to the Royal Society and the overseas applicant simultaneously submits a parallel application to the overseas funder.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure the overseas collaborator applies to their funder in the corresponding call and that both applications are coordinated; non-parallel submission may invalidate the cost-share arrangement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Country-specific named funding streams within Global rounds
rubrics_metrics.description: Global rounds include opportunities supported by specific funds: Yusuf and Farida Hamied Foundation (for collaborations with researchers in India), Sino-British Fellowship Trust (SBFT) (for collaborations with researchers in China), American Friends of the Royal Society (AFRS) (for collaborations with researchers in the USA).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If collaborating with researchers in these countries, indicate suitability for the named fund in your application and follow any extra guidance in the scheme notes about these funded streams.

rubrics_metrics.name: Application route and documentation
rubrics_metrics.description: You will apply through our application and grant management system, Flexi-Grant®. Full funding details can be found in the scheme notes for the Global round and the Cost Share rounds.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use Flexi‑Grant and consult the scheme notes and downloads (scheme notes, conditions of award) for required documents, templates, and full terms before submission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assessment process and reviewers
rubrics_metrics.description: Assessment is overseen by the International Exchanges Panel. Following eligibility checks, applications are reviewed and assessed by two members of the International Exchanges Panel who have the most appropriate scientific expertise. A shortlist is then drawn up with oversight from the Panel Chair to be recommended for funding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applications should be written with peer reviewers in mind: be clear, provide necessary scientific detail and justification, and show why the project fits the scheme objectives. Expect assessment by two subject‑expert panel members and shortlisting oversight by the Chair.

rubrics_metrics.name: Equity, diversity and inclusion (EDI) commitment
rubrics_metrics.description: The Royal Society recognises that diversity is essential for delivering excellence in STEM and wants to encourage applications from the widest range of backgrounds, perspectives and experiences to maximise innovation and creativity in science. We regularly review and revise policies and processes to embed EDI principles in all aspects of the grant making process and ensure all talented applicants have an equitable chance to succeed as per the assessment criteria.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants should be aware that EDI principles inform the assessment and selection process; if relevant, provide contextual information that may be considered under EDI policies (but note confidentiality rules regarding disability adjustments).

rubrics_metrics.name: Support and adjustments for disabled applicants
rubrics_metrics.description: Adjustments can include extension of the deadline; additional support to complete the application form; receiving the application form in a different format (such as on a Word document); support during interviews including technical support for accessibility software; additional costs candidates may incur to attend an interview.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requests for adjustments are made in confidence and will not normally be shared with panel members unless relevant to assessment. If sharing is necessary, permission will be sought. Contact the Grants team to arrange adjustments and indicate any required support early.

rubrics_metrics.name: Organisational ineligibility (excluded host organisations)
rubrics_metrics.description: Ineligible organisations include industrial, private and commercial organisations, university spin-out companies and government bodies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants employed by or proposing to use funding through ineligible organisations should note they cannot apply under this scheme; check employer status before applying.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of scheme notes and Conditions of Award
rubrics_metrics.description: Full funding details and further information are provided in the scheme notes and Conditions of Award.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants must read and comply with scheme notes and Conditions of Award; these documents contain detailed rules about eligibility, allowable costs, reporting and post-award conditions.
